s01: Round stones can make two different rhythms.
First, place them in straight rows.
Now let each row settle into the gaps below.
Their neighbors are still just touching.
But the rows can sit closer together.
Each pair is two radii apart.
Its height is the radius times the square root of three, instead of two.
A repeating cell keeps the same width.
Its height falls to about eighty seven percent.
The same circle area occupies less space around it.
Across a large repeating pattern, coverage rises from about seventy nine percent to ninety one percent.
Those numbers compare ideal equal circles in two repeating arrangements.
A small tray has edges, so its exact count is another question.
Look again at the staggered rows.
The quieter gaps are a consequence of a triangle.

scenes.narration:
Round stones can make two different rhythms. First, place them in straight rows. Now let each row settle into the gaps below.

The stones have not shrunk. Their neighbors are still just touching. But the rows can sit closer together.

Look at three neighboring centers. Each pair is two radii apart. They form an equilateral triangle. Split it down the middle. Its height is the radius times the square root of three, instead of two.

A repeating cell keeps the same width. Its height falls to about eighty seven percent. The same circle area occupies less space around it. Across a large repeating pattern, coverage rises from about seventy nine percent to ninety one percent.

Those numbers compare ideal equal circles in two repeating arrangements. A small tray has edges, so its exact count is another question. Look again at the staggered rows. The quieter gaps are a consequence of a triangle.
